claims.text: Removing one or more elements from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni changes local chemical short-range order.
Removing one or more elements from equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni changes lattice distortion.
Local chemical ordering and lattice distortion modulate dislocation interactions.
Local chemical ordering and lattice distortion modulate stacking-fault energy.
The resulting microstructural variations alter room-temperature strain hardening and ductility.
All compared alloys are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Identical thermomechanical processing ensures comparable grain sizes among the alloys.
Identical thermomechanical processing ensures comparable defect structures among the alloys.
Composition-induced changes in ordering and lattice distortion modify dislocation mobility.
Composition-induced changes in ordering and lattice distortion modify activation of slip systems.
Changes in dislocation mobility and slip-system activation affect strain hardening.
Changes in dislocation mobility and slip-system activation affect the onset of necking.
Equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets will have lower strain-hardening rates than the quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline under identical test conditions.
Equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets will have lower ductility than the quinary baseline.
Equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets will neck and fail earlier than the quinary baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies when the alloys remain single-phase FCC and free of second phases during room-temperature testing at a fixed strain rate.
